meeting_header:
Date: 2027-11-21
Time: 16:00 - 16:52 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Platform: Zoom (recording + transcript)
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Oliver Reed (Redwood SE), Sam Torres (Redwood SE), Jenna Morales (Azura Head of Procurement), Ravi Singh (Azura CISO), Laura Kim (Azura Legal), Tom Baker (Azura Infrastructure), Evan Lee (Azura Product)
summary: Procurement and legal alignment call to validate vendor gate criteria for Azura Health: MSA/DPA redlines, required SLA minima, data escrow expectations, KMS/SSO/KPI items, and timing for pricing/PO sign-off. High-level agreement on pilot + escrow + next legal redline exchange; technical runbook and pilot SLOs to follow.
topics: MSA redlines and acceptable liability cap
DPA and data residency / data classification requirements
Data escrow and escrow agent/triggering events
SLA targets (p99 latency, uptime) and remedies/credits
KMS / BYOK / HSM options and key rotation
Pricing approvals, PO timing, and pilot economics
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we have about 50 minutes, so we'll run through a quick vendor gate checklist then open for legal/tech questions.
[00:12] Jenna: Great, thanks. We just want to be clear on what exactly triggers the gate - is it PO + signed MSA or do you need SOC 2 report first?
[00:20] Maya: Good question. Our normal flow is PO + signed MSA, we put SOC 2 in as an attachment / attestation, and we can provide the report under NDA. For Azura, we can also do a conditional pilot before full-go as long as the DPA is in place.
[00:35] Ravi: Conditionals... okay. From security we need crypto controls around keys and explicit egress map. If you offer BYOK, what's the KMS model?
[00:44] Oliver: We support customer-managed keys via standard KMS providers and HSM workflows. There's a few implementation paths: Redwood-hosted KMS with envelope encryption, or customer keys in their cloud KMS with an integration we call BYOK. There's some perf tradeoffs in crypto path but it's supported.
[01:05] Tom: Sorry to jump in, is there an option where we keep the KV cache on-prem? We have latency sensitive flows for clinical triage.
[01:12] Sam: Speaker note - Kv-cache phrasing sometimes shows up, we can do dedicated capacity (Redwood Dedicated) which pins GPUs in region and reduces latency and keeps data isolated. That would be the recommended route for low-latency clinical inference.
[01:28] Laura: On the legal side, my team will need to see indemnity and liability caps. Standardly we ask for 1x to 3x of fees as cap or $10M, which is what our procurement playbook uses. Where do you typically land?
[01:40] Maya: For enterprise we usually land at a liability cap tied to fees for hosted API — often 1x annual fees; for Dedicated or Private we look at a higher cap and limited carveouts. But we can discuss specific numbers.
[01:52] Laura: Also data escrow -- we want an escrow that covers model weights and customer data at termination. Triggering events: insolvency or failure to deliver SLA for 30 days.
[02:03] Maya: Understood. We can include escrow language. Important clarifier: model weights vs customer prompts/derived data - we typically escrow customer owned artifacts and agreed artifacts, not proprietary open-source models. We'll propose language.
[02:18] Ravi: I want to call out audit logs and WORM storage, do you provide immutable logs for access?
[02:25] Oliver: Yes we have audit logging per tenant; retention is configurable. For Private deployments we can ship logs to your Splunk/Datadog. For hosted we'll retain logs for the agreed period and can export on request.
[02:38] Jenna: Pricing question: procurement needs to know if there's any egress fee or storage fee hidden after pilot.
[02:44] Maya: We put egress on in cases where customers pull large volumes out of our network; typically most customers don't hit egress charges for API usage, but for dedicated S3 syncs or raw model artifacts you might see transfer costs. We will call these out explicitly in the pricing sheet we send.
[02:58] Evan: Is there an escrow cost? Do vendors charge for escrow deposits or monthly fees?
[03:03] Maya: There's usually an annual escrow fee — varies by escrow agent and the artifacts being held. We can get you an estimate.
[03:10] Laura: On DPA, our compliance requires data classification: PHI cannot leave region and needs to be encrypted at rest with keys under our control. Is Redwood able to do region-restricted hosting?
[03:21] Oliver: Yes, we support region pinning with dedicated or private deployment and can integrate with your KMS for key control. For hosted API there are region-specific endpoints and data residency options but the strongest guarantee is Dedicated/Private.
[03:36] Ravi: About SLA metrics: we need p99 latency under 300ms for inference on the primary route and 99.95% uptime. What are your standard SLOs?
[03:46] Sam: Our public SLA for hosted is 99.9% with SLOs tuned per-model and per-route. For Dedicated we can negotiate 99.95% with capacity commitments and fallback policies. P99 latency depends on model/size; we can profile with a short benchmark.
[04:00] Tom: If we move to Dedicated, what happens if you can't meet throughput during spike? Auto-burst? Fallback to smaller model? We need predictable degrade behavior.
[04:09] Oliver: We configure automated fallback policies — routing to a quantized variant or a regional fallback. For guaranteed throughput you set reserved capacity and burst buffer. Those are usually captured in the SLA and runbook.
[04:22] Jenna: For procurement checklist, we need: signed MSA, DPA with Azura redlines, SOC2 report, price schedule, PO. Anything else?
[04:31] Maya: Also we add a security questionnaire (we'll send our standard sec pack), and the technical runbook for onboarding.
[04:37] Laura: On IP: we need a carveout that derivative outputs are Azura's, not Redwood's, and any models trained on Azura data are under Azura's control.
[04:46] Maya: We can accept a use-case-limited IP assignment for customer data derivatives; full model retraining on customer data has separate commercial terms. We'll flag that in the MSA proposal.
[04:58] Ravi: Escrow agent: do you have a preferred agent? We prefer one with healthcare experience.
[05:04] Maya: We typically work with Ironclad escrow partners and can propose two options that are used in enterprise deals; we'll include the agent and sample clause.
[05:12] Evan: Timelines — procurement needs top-level dates. What's reasonable between initial MSA and production?
[05:18] Maya: Typical is 4-8 weeks depending on redlines and SOC2/attestation availability. Pilot can begin earlier under DPA only, but we ask for a PO for pilot expenses.
[05:28] Jenna: For internal sign-off we will need price certainty. Can you commit to not increasing rates during the first 12 months of the agreement?
[05:36] Maya: Yes we can include price protection for the first year in the SOW.
[05:41] Laura: On remedies, we need a well-defined credit formula tied to downtime.
[05:46] Sam: We'll propose a tiered credit schedule aligned with SLA misses in the MSA appendix.
[05:51] Tom: Technical ask — can you show us an example runbook for a production cutover? That will help infra sign-off.
[05:58] Oliver: We'll prepare a runbook with sequence: cert exchange, VPC peering, routing, run-of requests, KV warm-up and traffic cutover steps.
[06:10] Jenna: ok let's confirm next steps and due dates.
[06:13] Maya: Recap: Redwood to send MSA + DPA with proposed escrow clause by 11/24. Laura to return mandatory redlines by 11/28. Tom/OIiver runbook session week of 11/29. Jenna to confirm procurement timing by 12/01. Any other items?
[06:28] Laura: Please include a clear list of what will be escrowed and the trigger events.
[06:31] Maya: Will do.
[06:33] Evan: One more question — are there any competitor items we should know that change terms?
[06:37] Maya: We've seen customers push for broader IP rights with some providers, and some competitors bundling model licensing. Redwood focuses on predictable serving + observability rather than model ownership; we'll call that out in the SOW.
[06:49] Ravi: Alright thanks all.
[06:51] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via email and upload the docs to the shared folder.
[06:56] (end)
file_notes: Transcript includes a few imperfect attributions (Speaker 1), and occasional ASR mis-hearings (Kv-cache spelled as KV cache/kv cash in raw). References to escrow agent and BYOK are approximate. This call is procurement/legal heavy; treat as medium transcription quality.
